value_play.note: SEARCH SHAPE + MULLIGAN-GEN SETTINGS. This deck ships NO value leaf and this file carries NO eval_model. Since 2026-10-15 it DOES change play: `ladder: single`, `leaf: none`, `alpha: relaxed` select the leafless single FIT pass (docs/design/per-deck-search-shape.md, menu shape #3), adopted by the USER after the 2026-10-14/15 value-leaf run measured it against the previous play (no sidecar shape): 8 held-out seeds x 1000 games, -0.0035 turns (paired t -3.13, 6 better / 1 worse / 1 tied), 0.895x work units; it also holds at the low-budget d3/b10 setting (-0.0016, t -2.60, 0.982x units). The trained model leaf was measured and NOT shipped (-0.0040 at ~1.35x real cost). The mull_gen_* keys below are MULLIGAN-GEN settings only and are unchanged by that adoption; the original justification follows. `target_depth` is deliberately ABSENT, which is what keeps value_play.present()/drives() false (MulliganProfileIO.h's note: 'a presence-only sidecar may carry JUST the mull_gen_* overrides'). `expected_buckets: 17` is the USER's bucket ruling (2026-10-15: 'K=17 seems to be correct. I already confirmed it for the previous generation'): it matches the shipped keep table and phase F's discovery on the adopted play, and it is recorded by the user, never by a derivation. WHY IT EXISTS: without it, src/analyzer/main.cpp's MullGenDepth(5)/MullGenBudgetMs(20) fall through to the BUILT-IN GEN DEFAULT, and logs/Snow_mullgen/gen.log shows the cancelled 2026-09-24 run did exactly that ('rollout depth: 5 (source: gen-default)'). That is the most expensive labeller setting any deck in this repo uses -- mull_gen_depth is 1 on 12 of 23 decks, mull_gen_budget_ms is 3 on 18 of 23 -- applied to the least tractable deck, and it is where the ~138 h FAST projection and the 30 s / 52 s / 161 s single rollouts in that log come from. DERIVED 2026-09-25 by the prescribed comp-scorer hand-mode sweep (docs/design/fivecolour-mullgen-labeller-sweep.md; MTG_SCORE_HANDS=200, R=30, paired hands across arms), scored on RANK fidelity against the d5/b20 reference rather than on the mean, because a uniform shift flips no keep and dispersion does. Play side: d5/b20 52,189 units/rollout; d3/b20 IDENTICAL ranking (rho 1.0000, dispersion 0.0000) at 1.04x, so depth 5 buys literally nothing over 3 -- the budget binds first. d3/b10 1.72x, d3/b3 2.48x, d2/b1 2.87x, d1/b1 2.90x, and EVERY one of those keeps 100.0% pairwise ordering agreement on 11,378 reference-separated pairs with rho >= 0.9984 and dispersion <= 0.030 turns (draw side agrees). d0/b0 is a cliff -- rho 0.9125, dispersion 0.3408, 97.4% agreement, +0.57 turn shift -- so the greedy labeller is NOT usable. d2/b1 is the pick: within 1% of the cheapest arm, slightly better dispersion than d1/b1 (0.0294 vs 0.0303 play, 0.0255 vs 0.0258 draw), and the same setting the FiveColour precedent chose. Cost: 2.87x fewer work units, 8m11s -> 3m27s wall on the 200-hand battery. NOTE this does NOT re-bucket the deck: discovery deliberately runs at shipped play settings, not mull_gen_* (the 2026-08-15 split), so K stays 17.
